newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bamerindus in merger talks - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Bamerindus in merger talks - newspaper.

text.p: Ailing Brazilian bank Bamerindus is holding talks with private bank Banco Safra on a possible merger, O Globo daily said on Friday.

Although Bamerindus and Banco Safra officially deny any deal, the newspaper said negotiations have been carried out secretly by Banco Safra's top executives, Carlos Alberto Vieira and Jose Inacio Puga.
In recent months Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth-largest private bank, has been the subject of speculation that it would be sold.
The sale of a controlling interest or merger with another bank is seen as the best solution for Bamerindus, which has been struggling to overcome liquidity troubles and restore public confidence.
In the last few weeks Bamerindus has been negotiating with the Central Bank a 90-day credit line, which newspapers reported would be worth $2.0-$3.0 billion, to solve its liquidity problems.

O Globo said the Central Bank is unwilling to grant any financial assistance to Bamerindus without a change of ownership, a move the bank's majority shareholder Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira has so far refused to accept.
The newspaper said Banco Safra is willing to acquire a bank in order to increase its market share, focusing on retail activities.
Bamerindus is a retail bank with an extensive branch network.
